annotations.text:
A — Dark: the brand as it already is.

The site's own palette, and the only one of the three that argues its case — an example answer, three claims, then the code. Best where people are already stopped at the table.

Trade-off: an A4 of near-black drinks ink and prints streaky on a desktop printer. Get this one run off at a print shop.

B — Paper: the same argument, printable at home.

One flat teal block instead of a full-bleed dark ground. Reads best under bright hall lighting and still works photocopied in black and white.

Trade-off: less arresting from a distance than A or C.

C — Scan first: for the aisle, not the table.

One instruction, one code, sized to be read and acted on from across a hall. At three metres there is nothing to read but the headline and the domain.

Trade-off: it says almost nothing about what the site does — it needs A beside it, or you doing the explaining.
